term: practical good and evil in the first precept of natural law
definition: Practical good concerns what practical reason apprehends as human goods to be pursued, in the order of natural inclinations; practical evil is contrary and to be avoided. The first precept is represented by GoodAct a → ToBePursued a and EvilAct a → ToBeAvoided a. These primitive predicates on acts are not defined by the ontological GoodIn relation on a being and a perfection, and no reduction of one to the other follows from juxtaposing them in a theory bundle.
